new_entities.name: Maternal psychological stress during pregnancy
new_entities.description: Psychological stress exposure during pregnancy, including major life stressors and maternal distress.

edges.effect_quant: The strongest pooled signal is a modest increase in childhood atopic dermatitis after prenatal maternal distress, but individual cohorts do not all agree on effect size or persistence.
edges.population: children exposed to maternal stress during pregnancy
edges.mechanism: Prenatal stress can alter fetal glucocorticoid exposure and early immune programming in ways that plausibly shift barrier and atopic vulnerability upward. That gives this edge a coherent developmental mechanism even though the human data are still mostly observational.
edges.summary: The meta-analysis is directionally clear: prenatal maternal distress is associated with more atopic dermatitis in offspring. What tempers the claim is that some later cohorts are smaller or null, so the right framing is a plausible risk amplifier rather than a stand-alone cause.
edges.caveats: Stress is measured very differently across studies and is tightly entangled with social adversity, sleep, and other maternal-health factors. That makes the direction more believable than the exact size of the effect.

evidence.citation: Flanigan C et al 2018 Clin Exp Allergy
evidence.notes: Prenatal maternal psychosocial stress and offspring's asthma and allergic disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

evidence.citation: Zhu TT et al 2024 Clin Transl Allergy
evidence.notes: Early exposure to maternal stress and risk for atopic dermatitis in children: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: maternal distress exposure versus lower or no distress
